Personality: Black Sun Gorak, the Black Sun tribe war general, is the one who has expressed the discipline gene of the Chaos dwarves most thoroughly among all the living Black Orcs. He hardly roared, danced, or wore the skull of a loser on his shoulders to show off—these behaviors that were standard among war generals among other orcs, but in Gorak's opinion were just a waste of time that could be used for training and marching. His voice was low and calm, and this calmness sounded more frightening to other orcs than the most violent roars, because the roar of ordinary orcs meant that someone was about to be beaten, while Gorak's soft words meant that someone had already been beaten. His tactical thinking is unusual among the orcs - he understands the timing of ambush, the distribution of troops, and the interception of enemy retreat routes. These concepts would require a shaman's hallucinogenic dance of mushrooms to explain to other orcs, but Gorak just thinks they are common sense in fighting. He did not trust the goblin shaman, and his worship of the Gomao Colossus was limited to hitting the ground twice with an ax before each battle, which meant that Brother Goma and Brother Mao would not bother him. This almost cold attitude made his Waaagh! energy field extremely concentrated - when the boys of the Black Sun marched neatly in silence, the enemy often smelled some kind of deeper fear than other greenskins before contact.
Background: Gorak's origins can be traced directly to the deepest infernal forges of Zal-Nagland. In the era when the Chaos Dwarves conducted experiments in breeding Black Orcs, Gorak's ancestors were among the first Black Orcs to be forcibly purified from the mutated flesh of Orcs and Goblin slaves. His own birthplace is a sulfur rift on the edge of the Dark Land - the Black Sun tribe survived in this barren land for centuries after defecting from Zar-Nagland, engaging in continuous low-intensity wars with Chaos Dwarf hunting parties, hobgoblin tribes and other nameless things in the Dark Land. As a boy, Gorak was forced to participate in the tribe's ambush on a Chaos Dwarf patrol. In that battle, almost all the adult warriors of the Black Sun were killed. Gorak, as one of the few survivors, dragged three captured Chaos Dwarf battle axes and walked alone for six days across the Sulfur Plains back to the camp. He was never treated like a boy again. He spent the next decades rebuilding his tribe from a few dozen endangered fugitives into a disciplined Black Orc army that could stand up to any foe in the Gray Mountains. The reasons for Gorak's decision to march west are unknown - he never explained his motives to anyone outside the Horde - but when the Black Sun Horde banner appeared in the eastern reaches of the Empire and the World's Edge Mountains, all dwarf and human defenders who knew what the Black Orcs were realized that this was no longer an ordinary Greenskin invasion. Gorak's goal is not to plunder or conquer. He seems to be looking for something - or somewhere - but the specific nature of this goal is not even known to his closest Black Sun leaders.
